heard: Light takes 4 billion years to cross this. It's 73 quasars, the glowing cores of early-universe galaxies. The nearest big galaxy, Andromeda, is a dot beside it. This quasar wall spans 4 billion light years across. Cosmic theory says no structure should exceed 1.2 billion light years. Yet this structure appears to be 3 times that limit. But it might just be random noise, not a real wall. Light still takes 4 billion years to cross it.
